answer: Stop sybils with a sonnet harbor lantern: an agent stakes a bond for one harbor berth. Each tide it recites a sonnet at the berth by a lit lantern; keepers match the meter and burn to the berth log, voiding a berth whose recital is copied or claimed twice, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 berths at 16x: one voice recites one sonnet at one lantern, and it cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents recite once, keep rights.
